title: Australopithecus sediba
summary: Australopithecus sediba is a hominin known from fossil skeletons found at Malapa, South Africa, first discovered in 2008 and dated to about 1.977 million years ago. The skeletons are unusually complete and mix features of Australopithecus with features of Homo, which fuels debate over the species' place in human evolution.

uncertainty.note: Smithsonian gives 1.977 to 1.98 million years ago; Pickering et al. give 1.977 ± 0.002 Ma for the Malapa fossils. Discovery year 2008.
